newsitem.title: INDIA: Fuel price hike prospects push down Delhi shares.
newsitem.headline: Fuel price hike prospects push down Delhi shares.

text.p: Prospects of an imminent petroleum price hike kept investors on the sidelines as Delhi share prices opened a shade lower in cautious early trade on Tuesday, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index was 1.53 points lower at 771.97 after 30 minutes of trade.
"Fears of hike in petroleum prices are keeping the buyers away from the market," said one broker.
The ruling United Front coalitions's steering committee will meet on May 25, and oil prices are expected to be the main issue.
India's oil pool deficit rose to 155 billion rupees ($4.33 billion) at the end of 1996/97 (April-March).

The deficit -- the money owed by the government to the oil companies for oil products below market prices -- will hit 245 billion rupees by the end of this fiscal year if nothing is done, according to junior Petroleum Minister T.R Balu.
"Players have adopted a cautious approach," said Ramesh Chander of brokers Vashisht Securities.
Reliance Industries quoted 0.65 rupee lower at 292.50 on scattered selling by speculators, brokers said.
State Bank of India dropped 1.15 rupee to 302.75 on profit-taking.
